newsitem.title: USA: North Carolina hearing on Liggett papers postponed.
newsitem.headline: North Carolina hearing on Liggett papers postponed.

text.p: A hearing on a temporary restraining order against distribution of Liggett Group tobacco documents has been put off until April 7, a spokeswoman for RJ Reynolds Tobacco Co said on Thursday.
The hearing in Forsythe County Court had been scheduled for Monday morning in Winston-Salem.

Tobacco companies secured the order a week ago, when Liggett, the fifth-largest U.S. tobacco business, owned by Brooke Group Ltd, struck a sweeping deal with 22 state governments suing cigarette makers to recover healthcare expenditures on sick smokers.
Liggett promised to turn over five boxes of internal documents, including some from industry meetings, which anti-tobacco lawyers say will bolster their claims against tobacco companies.

Judges in Florida, Illinois, Mississippi and Texas have since ordered Liggett to produce the documents, largely for private judicial review to ensure the client-lawyer privileges of tobacco companies are not violated by the disclosures.
Peggy Carter, spokeswoman for RJ Reynolds, a unit of RJR Nabisco, said the North Carolina hearing may be put back still further to April 8.
